text:
maria: quick heads-up — after yesterday's prefill/decode split we've been seeing a small regression on 2x GPU hosts for short-chat workloads.
aj: saw the dashboard alert, thanks. how big of a regression?
maria: p95 latency up ~8% and token throughput down ~4% on olivine-small profile with kv-priming enabled.
devon: can you paste the perfbot trace? I want to see where time is going.
perfbot: trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/trace/3495001234 — peaks during handshake+kv-warmup stage
sam: hmm that's the stage-aware scheduler we landed last week, right? could be token budget target too.
maria: right. hypothesis: separating prefill and decode batches increased handshake churn; KV cache priming now fires more often because small prefill batches don't keep the KV hot.
aj: makes sense — smaller prefill batches => more frequent kv priming across micro-batches.
devon: data: from the run logs
```
stage	avg_ms	count
prefill	12.1	20432
decode	8.9	48012
handshake	6.2	29012
kv_init	3.7	29012
```
sam: interesting kv_init coincides with handshake spikes — probably cache drains between isolated prefill ops.
maria: experiment idea: add a small token-budget buffer for prefill so it will coalesce tiny prefill-only requests for ~2ms before flushing to kernel. basically soft-hold to improve batch formation.
aj: can be a heuristic: if prefill_len < 8 tokens and queue depth < X, wait up to Y ms, else immediate.
devon: we tried a similar delay for decode earlier and saw tail latency surgery, but this is prefill so maybe OK.
perfbot: quick A/B: delta after 2ms hold: p95 back to baseline, throughput +2.5%, kv_init events down 48%.
sam: nice! is there a cost for heavy tail cases where hold causes extra latency for single-request flows?
maria: slight median increase for tiny single-users (~1.5ms), but p95 improved and throughput better overall.
aj: we should also feed kernel_selector with phase hint so it can pick lower-latency kernels for short prefill batches.
devon: agree — add a Phase enum in the request metadata: {phase: "PREFILL"} and let kernel_selector prefer prefill-optimized kernels.
maria: done a micropatch in the runtime: when phase==PREFILL and prefill_tokens<16, prefer kernel family A (faster small-seq path). keeps decode unchanged.
aj: that's great. any regressions in big-seq workloads?
perfbot: run summary on long-context tests: negligible difference (<0.2%).
sam: ok to roll to canary? propose canary to 10% for 24h.
maria: +1. will add rollout with auto-rollback if p95 regresses >5%.
devon: also add a KV warmup grace: keep per-GPU kv-hotset pinned for 50ms after the last prefill of that session to avoid immediate cold misses.
aj: that + phase hint + soft-hold seems like a good bundle.
perfbot: canary started at 2026-03-18T12:04Z to 10% — monitoring hooks active.
maria: I'll monitor cost and latency dashboards. thanks everyone :pray:
sam: if canary looks good we can include in tomorrow's release candidate.
aj: tagging infra oncall in case kernel_selector change needs quick rollback @devon
devon: on it, will keep an eye.
perfbot: note: captured a couple of sample traces for postmortem if needed: /artifacts/3495001234/*.json
maria: ok closing the loop — follow-up PR with metrics and config defaults coming up.
